name: Busan
coordsNote: City centre (Busan City Hall / Yeonsan area). Long-stay areas are Haeundae (beach, about 12 km east), Gwangalli (beach) and Seomyeon (downtown hub).

US.note: Visa-free up to 90 days. K-ETA temporarily waived until 31 Dec 2026; check whether the waiver is extended for 2027.

UK.note: Visa-free up to 90 days. K-ETA temporarily waived until 31 Dec 2026.

EU.note: Most EU nationals visa-free up to 90 days. The K-ETA waiver through 31 Dec 2026 covers only Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Sweden; other EU nationals need a K-ETA (KRW 10,000).

AU.note: Visa-free up to 90 days. K-ETA temporarily waived until 31 Dec 2026.

english.rationale: EF EPI 2025 puts South Korea at 522 (rank 48, Moderate band) and Busan's city score at 520. Signage and transit are fully bilingual, but spoken English outside hotels, Haeundae and younger crowds is limited. Same tier as Taipei and Osaka.

vibe: Korea's port city: urban beaches, seafood markets, hillside villages and an easy metro
narrative: Haeundae and Gwangalli put city beaches on the metro, with Jagalchi fish market, the painted hillside lanes of Gamcheon Culture Village and the seaside Haedong Yonggungsa temple in between. Spring and autumn are the long-stay months (the film festival is in October); July to September brings humidity, monsoon rains and typhoon risk.

season.rationale: Editorial estimate. The beach season is the domestic peak: Busan's beaches drew 21.46M visits in summer 2026, and Haeundae was open 26 June to 15 September. Spring blossom (Apr–May), Chuseok (Sep) and the film festival (Oct) keep those months busy. Winter (Dec–Feb) is quiet apart from Lunar New Year.

safety.propertyNote: Very low crime; occasional theft in crowds and nightlife areas
safety.womensSafetyNote: Women report high public-space safety; hidden-camera concerns
safety.touristRationale: Very low street crime; visitor issues are mostly nightlife-area incidents

rationale.property: Editorial estimate. The FCDO says theft against foreigners is rare and limited to crowded tourist and nightlife zones. Busan is Korea's second city and port, with marginally more nightlife and port-area friction than Osaka, so it's set just above Osaka (83) and below Tokyo (86) and Taipei (88).
rationale.tourist: No visitor-specific risk pattern beyond the nightlife-area assaults the FCDO mentions, so the modifier stays at 1.0.
rationale.womens: +5 over the national Gallup baseline, the same delta as Taipei: well-lit, CCTV-dense, busy public spaces. Kept below Osaka (+11) because of Korea's documented hidden-camera ('molka') problem and the FCDO's note on assaults around bars.

consulted.title: UK FCDO: South Korea safety and security
consulted.quote: There have been cases of assault, including sexual assault, particularly around bars and nightlife areas.

consulted.title: U.S. State Dept travel advisories feed (cadataapi.state.gov)
consulted.quote: consular services, including passport services, are not available at the U.S. Consulate in Busan
consulted.note: Official State Dept JSON feed; travel.state.gov itself served a Cloudflare bot challenge

selection: Korea's second city (the catalog has no Korean city yet): urban beaches, strong spring and autumn shoulder months, an October film festival, and a workation-friendly base with 90-day visa-free entry.
researchNotes: Advisory: travel.state.gov served a Cloudflare challenge, which was not bypassed. Level and date were read from the State Department's cadataapi feed: 'South Korea - Level 1: Exercise Normal Precautions', Published 2025-05-27T20:00-04:00, recorded as 2025-05-28 per the existing convention. The page mentions demonstrations, peninsula tensions and civil-defence drills but no risk-indicator letters. Visa: the K-ETA waiver ends 31 Dec 2026. If it isn't extended, US/UK/AU and the 11 exempt EU nationals will need a K-ETA (KRW 10,000) for 2027 stays. Australia's 90-day visa-free period wasn't confirmed on an Australian government page (smartraveller.gov.au timed out). The K-ETA exemption list does include Australia.
